items.title: Private sector bears bulk of Bhotekoshi flood losses
items.summary: A preliminary government assessment estimates damage and economic losses at Rs408 billion. Nearly 4,800 businesses and 7,570 homes were damaged, while 13 hydropower projects and five solar plants were hit.

items.title: Flood survivors face water shortages, disease risk in crowded holding centres
items.summary: More than 3,600 people are staying in 37 holding centres across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts. No major outbreak has been reported, but cases of colds, coughs and viral fever are common.

items.title: US approves $1m forensic support for Nepal flood victim identification
items.summary: The new funding takes US humanitarian, health and forensic assistance following the floods to more than $5 million.

items.title: Beijing signals support for rebuilding flood-ravaged Rasuwagadhi route
items.summary: Nepal has sought Chinese assistance to rebuild the 16-km Syaphrubesi-Rasuwagadhi road, while the government prepares a temporary track to restore access to the border crossing.

items.title: Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal on rebuilding after the Bhotekoshi floods
items.summary: The infrastructure development minister discusses plans for resettlement, damaged roads and bridges, the China border crossing and efforts to build safer settlements for disaster-prone communities.

items.title: Why Nepal’s climate crisis is also a public-health emergency
items.summary: The Bhotekoshi flood shows why Nepal’s climate crisis must also be understood as a public-health crisis.

items.title: The search dog helping find bodies buried by Nepal’s floods
items.summary: Samba, a Labrador trained to detect the scent of human remains, has helped rescuers locate around 20 bodies beneath mud and debris since the floods hit Rasuwa.

items.title: Flood damage leaves Rasuwagadhi road facing long repairs
items.summary: The Department of Roads is opening temporary tracks and planning Bailey bridges after the Bhotekoshi flood washed away about 40 km of road, while officials aim to restore a link to the Chinese border before Dashain.
